seoTitle: How to Give Jira Access to a User (Dashboard & Projects)
metaDescription: Invite new users to Jira, assign roles and permissions, and provide dashboard access to projects with this step-by-step guide.
intro: Onboarding a new teammate into Jira means more than just sending an invite — they also need the right role, permissions, and dashboard visibility. This guide covers how to add a new user, assign appropriate access, and share dashboards with them.

steps.heading: Invite the new user
steps.body: From your Jira admin settings, invite the new team member by entering their email address.

steps.heading: Assign roles and permissions
steps.body: Set the user's project role and permissions so they have access appropriate to their responsibilities.

steps.heading: Provide dashboard access
steps.body: Share the relevant dashboard with the user so they can view reports and metrics for their project.

steps.heading: Confirm project access
steps.body: Double-check the user can see and interact with the correct projects and boards after setup.

steps.heading: Follow access control best practices
steps.body: Grant only the permissions each user actually needs to keep your Jira instance secure and organized.

faq.question: Who can invite new users to Jira?
faq.answer: Typically only Jira or site administrators can invite new users and manage their permissions.

faq.question: Can I limit a user to just one project?
faq.answer: Yes, you can assign project-specific roles so a user only has access to the projects you grant them.

faq.question: How do I share a dashboard with a specific user?
faq.answer: Use the dashboard's share settings to add the individual user, a group, or the whole project to its viewer list.

faq.question: What happens if I remove a user's access?
faq.answer: Removing access revokes their ability to view or edit the project and dashboard, though their historical activity remains logged.
